entrypoints.summary: An attacker places an image URL referencing an externally hosted SVG in a GitLab issue description; an enabled asset proxy fetches and serves the content from its proxy origin.

negative_controls: A CSP including form-action 'none' is the documented configuration intended to block form submission.
No runtime browser trace or HTTP capture is present in the supplied bundle.
observability.positive_marker: The form submission sends entered data to the selected external endpoint, exemplified as example.com in the report.

preconditions: A GitLab deployment has asset proxying enabled.
The proxy serves attacker-hosted SVG image content.
The proxy CSP does not restrict form actions.
Credential-phishing escalation additionally depends on a self-hosted proxy under the instance parent domain and password-manager behavior.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: An img element referencing an externally hosted SVG that contains HTML form markup.
trigger_steps.summary: Create an issue containing an image reference to an attacker-hosted SVG with form content, open the proxy-served image, then fill and submit the rendered form.

sources.concept: attacker-controlled SVG embedded as issue image content

impact.affected_asset: Victim data entered into the rendered form; credential exposure is deployment- and password-manager-dependent rather than demonstrated as universal.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause a victim who opens a proxied attacker-controlled SVG to submit form data to an attacker-selected endpoint.
impact.security_effect: Form-based phishing and exfiltration of data entered by a victim into a form rendered from the proxy origin.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies an externally hosted SVG through an image reference in an issue description; the report states that the SVG can contain HTML form markup.
The asset proxy serves the attacker-controlled SVG under the proxy origin while the described proxy CSP configurations do not constrain form actions.
After a victim opens the proxy-served SVG, the rendered form can be filled and submitted to an attacker-selected endpoint.

The demonstrated outcome is outbound submission of victim-entered form data; the report identifies credential theft through password-manager autofill or auto-submit as conditional on self-hosted parent-domain deployment and password-manager behavior.

failure.operation: Browser form submission from proxy-served attacker-controlled SVG to an attacker-selected endpoint

primary_invariant.kind: browser CSP form-submission boundary for proxy-served untrusted content
primary_invariant.statement: Content served by an asset-proxy origin must not be able to submit HTML forms to external endpoints.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The report describes proxy CSP headers that omit a form-action restriction, allowing a form contained in attacker-hosted SVG content to submit after being served by the proxy.

quality.review_notes: The primary disclosure supplies a concrete setup and browser interaction sequence, but the bundle contains no malicious SVG fixture, response-header capture, browser/network trace, automated test, or observed test execution. The remediation is a merged documentation/configuration instruction, not evidence of GitLab- or proxy-code-enforced mitigation. Credential theft via password-manager autofill or auto-submit remains a conditional downstream claim.

remediation.invariant_restored: The supplied merged documentation directs asset-proxy operators to use a CSP including form-action 'none', preventing proxy-served content from submitting forms.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Asset-proxy-enabled GitLab deployments whose proxy CSP does not restrict form actions; the supplied remediation documentation was merged at commit bfd7a5c0af9f3098669b081e44de18151cc20661.

target.component: configured asset proxy server serving proxied image content

oracle.expected_negative: With the proxy CSP configured to include form-action 'none', browser form submission from the proxy-served SVG is blocked.
oracle.expected_positive: With an asset proxy enabled and no form-action restriction, opening a proxied attacker-controlled SVG exposes its form and submitting it sends the entered data to the selected external endpoint.
